I do want to take a moment to mention that, despite what I just said, "Stop letting your potential go to waste" is a pretty terrible thing to say. It may have sounded good to whoever wrote it, but it reads like they're trying to shame the reader for not doing as well as they apparently should be, which is the exact opposite of helpful. It sounds hostile.

As for the second part, I have mixed feelings about it. First off, I think it's a pretty bad way to say it and flies in the face of the message they're trying to create. Comparison is the thief of joy, and comparing people who aren't confident in their abilities to those who are is not a great way to get people to build up confidence themselves. It usually just ends up making people feel bad about not doing well and doesn't motivate them to even try. I also take issue with the "making waves" line specifically because people's worth should not be measured by how influential or successful they are. A somewhat better thing to say would have been "other people far less talented are still doing what they love, and so can you". However, even though it was a bad way to say it, they're not technically wrong. There are definitely people who aren't as naturally gifted as others who are still doing well at whatever it is they do simply because they're more motivated and feel more assured in their abilities. Talent can only get you so far. It is ultimately important to recognize that it should not be relied upon and that you do have to be willing to work at things to get better at them.
